# Implement version read + dimmed right-aligned header display

## Summary
Read the plugin version at runtime from `packages/herdr/package.json` and render it as a dimmed, right-aligned `v<version>` suffix in the work item selection list header, without disturbing the left-aligned title.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A runtime helper reads the plugin version from `packages/herdr/package.json` (JSON parse via `readFileSync`, following the `shortcut-config.ts` pattern); when the file is missing or unparseable it falls back gracefully (e.g. `'?'` or omit) without throwing.
- The list-mode header renders `v<version>` right-aligned to `cols` (visible-width padding computed with ANSI codes stripped before padding), dimmed via `ANSI.dim`, matching the `[auto-refresh on]` treatment; the left-aligned `Work Items — N item(s)` title is unchanged.
- The version is read at runtime from the manifest, not hardcoded in the renderer (stays in sync with the manifest version).
- On narrow panes where the suffix would overlap the title, the suffix is dropped or truncated (guard on `cols`) — no layout breakage, no overflow beyond the pane width.
- Full project test suite passes with the new changes, including the header version tests (F1).

## Minimal Implementation
- Add a small version-read helper in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` (or a sibling module) using the `readFileSync`/`dirname` pattern from `shortcut-config.ts`, with a safe fallback.
- In the list-mode header renderer (near line ~1585): compute the header's visible width, pad to `cols`, and append the dimmed `v<version>` suffix right-aligned; reuse `truncateLine`/visible-length logic; guard on `cols` for narrow panes.
- Keep the renderer testable via the existing `readFile`-style injection seam where practical.

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: header version rendering tests (F1) — test-first ordering.

## Deliverables
- Updated `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`; version helper; no change to `packages/herdr/package.json` (version source only).

# Extract worklist constants, types and layout

**Parent:** WL-0MVGKGD2Y0038S6B. **Phase:** 1 of 7 extraction slices (leaf modules).

## Target outcome

The three leaf modules of the split exist, carry the module-level doc comments
required by parent AC6, and `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` re-exports them from
its barrel position — no consumer or test change required.

## Scope (measured line ranges on the current `dev` tree)

| New module | Contents (current `worklist.ts` lines) | Est. size |
|---|---|---|
| `worklist.constants.ts` | Constants (164–224): `SHIP_IT_COMMAND`, `STAGES`/`Stage`, `STAGE_MAP`, `PRIORITY_MAP`, `STAGE_COLORS`; `ANSI` (345–368); mouse timing `DOUBLE_CLICK_WINDOW_MS`, `DRAG_THRESHOLD_CELLS` (3558–3592); any tooltip/chord tuning constants | ~170 |

| `worklist.layout.ts` | `MIN_META_SHARE`, `MAX_META_SHARE`, `computeMetadataPanelHeight`, `computeDynamicLayout` (226–316), `getTermSize` (327–344) | ~130 |

`worklist.types.ts` **must be a leaf**: type-only declarations, no imports from
any other `worklist.*` module (parent AC4 — this is what keeps later modules
cycle-free).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `worklist.constants.ts`, `worklist.types.ts` and `worklist.layout.ts` exist,
   each ≤1,000 lines, each opening with a doc comment stating its single
   responsibility (AC6).
2. Provenance comments move with their code: the `// ── Constants ──`,
   `// ── /wl <stage> argument map (WL-0MSDT8X1V003206G) ──`,
   `// ── /wl --priority <priority> map (WL-0MSKC8T46006999S) ──`,
   `// ── Metadata panel sizing ──`, `// ── Terminal helpers ──` banners and all
   inline work-item ids survive verbatim in the destination modules.
3. `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` re-exports the symbols in this slice that
   consumers actually use — `ANSI`, `SHIP_IT_COMMAND`, `STAGES`, `Stage`,
   `TermSize`, `getTermSize`, `computeMetadataPanelHeight`,
   `computeDynamicLayout`, `DOUBLE_CLICK_WINDOW_MS`, `DRAG_THRESHOLD_CELLS`,
   `DisplayRow`, `DisplayHeadingRow`, `ChordState`, `ParsedMouseEvent`,
   `MouseDragState`, `MouseClickState`, `MouseAction`. **Internal** (declared in
   the new modules, exported from them for sibling use, but *not* re-exported by
   the barrel, because no external consumer imports them): `KeyAction`,
   `HelpIconRow`, `NoteEditAction`, `ReviewQueueBannerState`, `PodcastNotice`,
   `ExecuteResult`, `PodcastTargetResolution`, `ViewMode`, `MIN_META_SHARE`,
   `MAX_META_SHARE`.
   *(Plan-time correction, 2026-10-30: the guarded symbol set is re-derived
from the live import scan — 66 symbols are imported by the 36 consumer
files. Every symbol listed as internal below is imported by no external
consumer, so parent AC2 requires it to stay module-private.)*
4. `worklist.split-guard.test.ts` is green: every baseline/consumer symbol still
   exported from `./worklist.js`, no worklist module imports the barrel at
   runtime, no new cycle, all modules ≤1,000 lines (AC4, AC1, AC2).
5. `tsc --noEmit` (or `npm run build` in `packages/herdr`) succeeds and the full
   `packages/herdr` suite passes with **no test-file changes** (AC3, AC9).
6. Documentation that names these symbols is updated to the new module paths:
   `packages/herdr/README.md` (module-layout block around line 2345 and the
   `ANSI`/colour references), `docs/COLOUR-MAPPING.md` (line 77) if the
   `formatItemLine` reference needs the new home (deferred there if format has
   not moved yet — record the deferral in a comment).
7. **Behaviour-preserving, move-only refactor.** No functional or logic change,
   no renames of public symbols, no behavioural diffs. No test file is modified —
   not its import paths, fixtures or assertions — and all 24 `worklist*.test.ts`
   suites (15,988 lines) plus the whole `packages/herdr` suite pass unchanged.
   → Owned by this slice: no test file is modified and the `packages/herdr` suite is green.
8. **No new circular imports.** Extracted modules import only from concrete
   sibling modules, never from the `worklist.js` barrel or from `index.ts`; the
   existing `worklist → fetcher/visibility/…` edge direction is preserved and no
   new cycle is introduced.
   → Owned by this slice: the guard's cycle gate reports no new circular import.
9. **Responsibility documented per module.** Each new module carries a
   module-level doc comment stating its single responsibility, and existing
   provenance comments (work-item ids, section banners such as
   `// ── Mouse / touch input (WL-0MSGHM5BQ0096BNJ) ──`) move with their code so
   traceability is preserved.
   → Owned by this slice: each module created here carries a responsibility doc comment and the moved provenance banners/comments are verbatim.

# Extract shared data-file push preamble helper

Refactor child of WL-0MVPUCVXL0099TND (*Deduplicate the worktree/push preamble
shared by `gitPushDataFileToBranch` and `rewriteAndForcePushDataFile`). Its
sibling *Pin push-path policy divergence with tests* lands the behavioural tests
first; this child performs the dedupe and must leave those tests untouched and
green.

## Why

`gitPushDataFileToBranch` (incremental) and `rewriteAndForcePushDataFile`
(rewrite) in `src/sync/push.ts` each carry a near-identical preamble:

1. cross-project guard (`assertDataFileInCwdRepo`)
2. `refs/heads/` + `refs/tags/` safety guard
3. `git rev-parse --git-dir`
4. repo-root / repo-relative-path resolution (`getRepoRoot`,
   `getRepoRelativePath`, `path.resolve`)
5. data-file existence check
6. `withTempWorktree(...)`
7. `ensureDir` + `copyFileSync`
8. `git add -f`
9. `git diff --cached`
10. `git commit`

A fix to any one of those steps must currently be made twice and can silently
drift.

## Desired change

One **private** helper in `src/sync/push.ts` (working name
`withDataFileInTempWorktree`) owns the preamble and delegates the
mode-specific tail to a callback:

- **Guard + resolve:** `assertDataFileInCwdRepo`, the refs rejection,
  `git rev-parse --git-dir`, `getRepoRoot()` / `getRepoRelativePath()` /
  `path.resolve()`, and the existence check.
- **Materialise:** `withTempWorktree(repoRootPath, target, …, { forceOrphan })`,
  `ensureDir` + `copyFileSync`, `add -f`, `diff --cached`.
- **Commit**, then invoke the caller's `run(worktreePath, relativePath, …)` so
  each caller performs only its own push and post-push bookkeeping.

The four documented behavioural differences must stay **explicit options**, not
collapsed:

- `emptyStage: 'skip' | 'throw'` — `'skip'` resolves as a no-op **without**
  invoking the callback; `'throw'` raises the existing
  `Nothing staged for the rewrite; aborting to avoid an empty ref` message.
- `missingFile: 'skip' | 'throw'` — `'skip'` returns silently; `'throw'` raises
  `Worklog data file not found: <path>`.
- `forceOrphan: boolean` — `true` only for the rewrite path.
- `skipPrePushHint: boolean` — `true` only for the incremental path, so both
  guard messages stay byte-identical to today.

The incremental path's foreign-tracked-file cleanup (`listTrackedFiles` +
`git rm` + `git clean -fdx`) stays in `gitPushDataFileToBranch`'s callback — it
is mode-specific, not preamble.

Both public functions then reduce to: resolve options → call the helper →
mode-specific push. The rewrite path additionally updates
`refs/worklog/remotes/<remote>/<branch>` and returns the new tip SHA.

## Constraints

- Pure refactor: no signature change, no behavioural change, no error-message
  change.
- No consumer edits; the `./sync.js` barrel surface is unchanged.
- The helper stays private to `src/sync/push.ts`; `src/sync/worktree.ts` stays a
  data-file-agnostic lifecycle layer and does not learn about data files.
- No scope creep into the duplicate read-side preamble in `src/sync/remote.ts`
  (record it as a separate follow-up if it is worth doing).
- Agent test runs go through `/skill:test` only.

## Risks to keep pinned

- **Empty-stage drift (highest risk).** A single policy applied to both paths
  would either publish nothing while reporting success (rewrite) or turn a
  routine no-change sync into an error (incremental). The sibling's
  negative-proof tests fail if this happens.
- **Guard-message merge.** Collapsing the two messages would drop the
  `Use WORKLOG_SKIP_PRE_PUSH=1` hint from the incremental path (or add it where
  it does not belong). The hint is an explicit parameter; the exact-text test
  pins it.
- **Lost `forceOrphan`.** If the helper does not thread `{ forceOrphan: true }`
  through to `withTempWorktree`, the rewrite path fetches the polluted ref
  again — the exact bug the earlier split fixed.
- **Return-type widening.** The rewrite path needs a value from inside the
  callback (tip SHA) while the skip policy produces nothing. The helper's
  generic return must stay honest so the rewrite caller cannot silently drop
  the SHA.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Single shared preamble.** One new private helper (e.g. `withDataFileInTempWorktree`) in `src/sync/push.ts` contains the cross-project guard, the refs safety guard, `git rev-parse --git-dir`, the repo-root/relative-path resolution, the existence check, and the `withTempWorktree` + copy + `add -f` + `diff --cached` + commit sequence; both `gitPushDataFileToBranch` and `rewriteAndForcePushDataFile` are implemented on top of it. Each of those steps appears exactly once in the file (inspection / duplicate-block assertion), and `src/sync/push.ts` gets shorter.
  - The helper owns: `assertDataFileInCwdRepo`, the refs safety guard, `git rev-parse --git-dir`, `getRepoRoot`/`getRepoRelativePath`/`path.resolve`, the existence check, `withTempWorktree` + `ensureDir` + `copyFileSync` + `add -f` + `diff --cached` + `commit`.
  - The four documented differences stay explicit options: `emptyStage: 'skip' | 'throw'`, `missingFile: 'skip' | 'throw'`, `forceOrphan` (rewrite only), `skipPrePushHint` (incremental only).
  - The incremental path's foreign-tracked-file cleanup stays in `gitPushDataFileToBranch`'s callback; the rewrite path still returns the new tip SHA and updates `refs/worklog/remotes/<remote>/<branch>`.
  - Duplicate-block inspection: none of the ten preamble steps appears twice.

- **Behaviour preserved exactly, proven by test.** Named tests assert, for *both* paths: (a) rejection of `refs/heads/*` and `refs/tags/*` targets with today's message text (including the `Use WORKLOG_SKIP_PRE_PUSH=1` hint on the incremental path only); (b) the cross-project guard still fires; (c) the empty-stage policy — incremental path resolves without error, rewrite path rejects with `Nothing staged for the rewrite`; (d) the missing-data-file policy — incremental path resolves, rewrite path rejects with `Worklog data file not found`; (e) the push invocation carries `--no-verify` (incremental) and `--force --no-verify` (rewrite).
  - The sibling's tests (empty-stage, missing-file, refs messages, cross-project guard, push flags) pass unchanged and green after the refactor.
  - `{ forceOrphan: true }` is threaded to `withTempWorktree` on the rewrite path only; the pre-push hint appears on the incremental path only; the rewrite path cannot silently drop the tip SHA.

- **Size and structural gate.** `src/sync/push.ts` shrinks (net fewer lines); no file exceeds 1,000 lines; `tests/sync/split-guard.test.ts` is green with `tests/sync/sync.split-baseline.json` **unchanged** (no re-baselining); `npm run build` is green; `/skill:test` (changed scope) is green.
  - `src/sync/push.ts` net shorter; no file exceeds 1,000 lines.
  - `tests/sync/split-guard.test.ts` green with `tests/sync/sync.split-baseline.json` unchanged (no re-baselining).
  - `npm run build` green; `/skill:test` (changed scope) green.

- **No surface change.** The `src/sync.ts` barrel exports are identical (same names, same signatures — asserted by `tests/sync/split-guard.test.ts`); no consumer edits in `src/commands/sync.ts`, `src/commands/doctor.ts`, `src/commands/init.ts` or `src/index.ts`.
  - Barrel export names and signatures identical; no edits in `src/commands/sync.ts`, `src/commands/doctor.ts`, `src/commands/init.ts` or `src/index.ts`.

- **Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries — specifically the `src/sync/push.ts` module header (naming the helper and the two policies) and the `src/sync/push.ts` row/table entry in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` if its description changes. CHANGELOG.md is excluded (managed by the release pipeline).
  - `src/sync/push.ts` module header names the helper and the two mode-specific policies.
  - The `src/sync/push.ts` row in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` is updated if the module description changes; `CHANGELOG.md` untouched (release pipeline owns it).

- **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**
  - Enforced at the dev-push gate (pre-push hook runs `--scope full`).

## Key Files

- `src/sync/repo-context.ts` — Read only (unchanged): `assertDataFileInCwdRepo`,

- `src/sync.ts` — Unchanged barrel; verify the exports are identical.
- `tests/sync-worktree.test.ts` — Read only (must stay green).
- `tests/rewrite-and-force-push.test.ts` — Read only (must stay green).
- `tests/sync/split-guard.test.ts` — Read only (must stay green);

Facts captured at plan time (2026-10-30, `dev`, `worklist.ts` = 7,899 lines):

- **36 consumer files** import from `./worklist.js`/`./worklist`: 2 production
  (`index.ts` → `getTermSize`, `runWorklistTui`; `fetcher.ts` → `STAGES`,
  `Stage`) and 34 test files, of which **24** are `worklist*.test.ts` suites.
- **66 distinct symbols** are imported across those consumers; the other 23 of
  the 89 current exports are unused outside the module and become internal
  (parent AC2).
- `WorkItemListState` is declared **once** (`worklist.ts:490`) — the single
  owner AC5 protects.
- `runWorklistTui` is declared once (`worklist.ts:5581`, `export async function`)
  and must stay at the `./worklist.js` path with an identical signature
  (child WL-0MVND6MQS000L01W).
- The live static import graph already contains one large component that
  includes `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`
  (`CYCLE_BASELINE` in `packages/herdr/test/split-guard/scan.ts`). It is
  pre-existing and out of scope; what the gate forbids is a **new** cycle member
  or a new **runtime** cycle (parent AC4).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. New **additive** test file `packages/herdr/src/worklist.split-guard.test.ts`
   (vitest) exists and passes on the current tree **before any production code
   moves**; no existing test file is modified (parent AC3).
2. Committed baseline `packages/herdr/src/worklist.split-baseline.json` records
   the 66 consumer-imported symbol names plus provenance (generation command,
   source commit, timestamp, scanned globs).
3. **Public-surface gate:** every baseline symbol is still exported by
   `./worklist.js` (value or type), and every symbol the live consumers import
   from the barrel is exported by it — so a lost or trimmed re-export fails the
   suite (parent AC2).
4. **Single state-owner gate:** exactly one production
   `packages/herdr/src/worklist*.ts` module declares `WorkItemListState`
   (parent AC5), mirroring the `dispatchInFlightCount` gate.
5. **Barrel/cycle gate:** no production `worklist.*.ts` module contains a
   runtime (value) import of `./worklist.js` (nor of `./index.js`); the static
   import graph of `worklist*.ts` modules contains no cycle outside the recorded
   baseline allowlist (parent AC4).
6. **Size gate:** every production `packages/herdr/src/worklist*.ts` module is
   ≤1,000 lines, excluding an exported `SPLIT_ALLOWLIST` that initially contains
   only `'worklist.ts'`; a further assertion proves the allowlist only ever
   shrinks (it must remain a subset of the plan-time list). The final barrel
   child empties it (parent AC1).
7. Each gate is proven to fail on a deliberately broken input (a synthetic
   >1,000-line module, a dropped export, a runtime barrel import, a duplicated
   `WorkItemListState`, a new cycle) — the failure modes are unit-tested, not
   assumed.
8. **Reuse, do not fork, the scanner:** extend
   `packages/herdr/test/split-guard/scan.ts` minimally so the barrel path, the
   module-family matcher and the single-owner declaration name are injectable
   (each defaulting to today's `downtime-worker` behaviour). The existing
   `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.split-guard.test.ts` and
   `downtime-worker.split-baseline.json` must stay **byte-identical and green** —
   duplicating the 28k-line scanner is not acceptable.
9. `/skill:test` (changed scope) passes, including the new guard suite and the
   untouched `downtime-worker` guard.
10. A comment on this item records the baseline generation command and the
    gate-to-parent-AC mapping.

## Minimal implementation

1. Parametrise `packages/herdr/test/split-guard/scan.ts`: accept a
   `barrel`/`family`/`declarationName` target (defaults unchanged) in
   `isSplitFamilyFile`, `splitFamilyModules`, `findBarrelValueImports`,
   `findSplitFamilyCycles` and `findDispatchInFlightDeclarations`; add a
   `--target worklist` branch to the `--write-baseline` CLI.
2. Generate the baseline: scan `src/**/*.ts` + `packages/herdr/src/*.ts` for
   `import … from './worklist.js'`, normalise `type ` prefixes, dedupe, sort →
   `worklist.split-baseline.json` with provenance fields (expect 66 symbols).
3. Write `worklist.split-guard.test.ts` with the five gates (exports,
   single-owner, cycle/barrel, size+allowlist, baseline provenance), each as a
   separately named `it()` so failures are legible.
4. Add the negative-case fixtures (temp files under `os.tmpdir()` or inline
   sources parsed by the same helpers) and assert each gate reports a failure.
5. Export `SPLIT_ALLOWLIST` from the guard's helper section so the final child
   (`WL-0MVND6OOL004SK9N`) can empty it in one line.
6. Run `/skill:test` (changed scope); record the guard output in a comment.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.split-guard.test.ts` — new
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.split-baseline.json` — new
- `packages/herdr/test/split-guard/scan.ts` — minimal parametrisation (defaults preserved)
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — read-only (no edits in this child)

## Constraints

- Additive only: adding a test file and a parametrisation hook does not violate
  parent AC3 ("no test file is modified").
- No production `worklist*.ts` edits in this child — it lands first, alone.
- No new runtime dependencies (`typescript` is already used by `scan.ts`).

## Dependencies

None — first child; every extraction child is blocked by this one.

# Implement: thread uninitialised worklog notice into TUI

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — visible, persistent error instead of a silent blank list.** When no valid worklog root can be resolved for the pane's CWD, the selection-list TUI renders a persistent error line that names the uninitialised worklog (including the resolved path) and instructs the operator to run `wl init`. The pane must not render an empty list with no explanation. The line is re-rendered every frame while the state holds and disappears on a subsequent refresh once a valid worklog root is resolved.
- **AC2 — covers both missing and invalid `.worklog/`.** The error is shown whenever `resolveWorklogRoot()` returns `undefined`: a missing `.worklog/` and an existing but invalid `.worklog/` (for example only `worklog.db`, no `config.yaml`/`initialized`). It must not be shown when a valid root is resolved.
- **AC3 — canonical `wl init` wording; non-interactive diagnostic preserved.** Every user-facing uninitialised message uses the canonical command `wl init` (replacing the current `worklog init` text in `uninitializedReport()` and `formatWlError()`). The existing stderr diagnostic is retained for non-interactive / TUI-unavailable runs, using the same wording.
- **AC4 — testing/validation.** New or updated unit tests cover: (a) the error is present in the rendered output when the worklog root is unresolved and absent when it is resolved; (b) the explicit `wl init` wording; (c) the invalid/partial `.worklog/` case is treated as uninitialised. Tests live in `packages/herdr/src/index.test.ts` and the worklist renderer tests.

## Implementation Notes

- In `main()` (`packages/herdr/src/index.ts`): capture the start dir used for `configureWorklogTarget()`, and when `wlRoot` is `undefined`, call `uninitializedReport(startDir)` and pass the result to `runWorklistTui`.

- Fix copy in `uninitializedReport()` (`packages/herdr/src/index.settings.ts`) and `formatWlError()` (`packages/herdr/src/fetcher.args.ts`): `worklog init` → `wl init`.

- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — `main()` passes uninitialisedNotice to runWorklistTui.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.settings.ts` — `uninitializedReport()` copy fix.
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.args.ts` — `formatWlError()` copy fix.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `runWorklistTui` options + `createListRenderer` signature.

# Redirect post-push verification full-suite runs to a pinned isolated worktree

## Problem Statement

A full-suite run executed from the main checkout during post-push verification
can race with a sibling `implement.py finish` fast-forwarding the main
checkout's local `dev` (`git merge --ff-only`), swapping source files mid-run
and producing phantom failures (WL-0MVSLXT79008D4X6 evidence: 4 failures in
`tests/herdr/send-to-pi.test.ts` / `tests/herdr/settings.test.ts` at
1abe9618; identical tree green in an isolated worktree minutes earlier).

## Goal (User Story)

As an AI agent running `implement.py finish`, I want post-push verification and
audit cache-miss full-suite runs to execute in an isolated worktree pinned to
the pushed commit — never live in the main checkout — so a sibling finish
fast-forwarding `dev` cannot swap the files a suite is reading.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Mitigate the race:** the post-push verification path is updated so that
   full-suite runs execute in an isolated worktree against a pinned commit,
   and the cache entry is grafted into the main checkout — not run live in
   the main checkout where a sibling finish can fast-forward `dev` mid-run.
2. The post-push verification path (and the audit skill F3 cache-miss
   auto-execution path) resolves an isolated worktree for the commit being
   verified and executes the full suite there — not in the live main checkout
   where a sibling `finish` can fast-forward `dev` mid-run.
3. The fresh cache entry produced by the isolated-worktree run is grafted into
   the main checkout's `.worklog/cache` before/mirroring the pre-push hook's
   `mirror_suite_cache` semantics (never overwrites an existing entry), so
   read-only post-push verification and audits serve the grafted entry.
4. The mitigation is minimal and localised: document + redirect test execution
   to worktrees; it does not rewrite the post-push verification pipeline or
   change verdict semantics (`green`/`red`/`missing`/`not_applicable`).
5. The single-owner main-checkout flock lock (WL-0MVPE2DA7007WF84) and the
   main-checkout guard (WL-0MVPE2BY9001CR9O) remain intact; finish refuses
   loudly rather than masking a real failure.
6. The full project test suite passes with the change.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `phase_finish()` read-only
  verification step and Step-6 main-checkout dev fast-forward
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_run_tests_via_test_skill` /
  F3 auto-execution (`run_cached(..., cwd=per_audit_root)`)
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`, `skill/test_cache.py` — suite execution
  and cache
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — guidance to match

## Constraints

- Must not break the dev-push pre-push hook's cache mirroring
  (`mirror_suite_cache`, `src/doctor/hook-upgrade.ts` in ContextHub /
  `.githooks/pre-push`).
- The audit skill's F3 cache-miss path must be covered (audits running in the
  main checkout face the same race).
- Worktree creation cost is assumed negligible (node_modules is symlinked);
  latency must stay bounded.
- Implementation repo: framework skills live in the SorraAgents repo
  (`~/.pi/agent/skills` → `/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/skill`); run
  `wl` worktree-safely with `--worklog-dir` when operating there.

# Suppress known phantom test-failure patterns in triage

## Problem Statement

When the main checkout's `dev` is fast-forwarded mid-test-run by a sibling
`implement.py finish`, a suite produces failures that exist in **no single
commit** (tests from X, source from Y). The test-failure triage logic can mint
phantom `test-failure` work items from such mixed-tree output, creating noise
and false work for producers (WL-0MVSPZ1FH000RWET).

## Goal (User Story)

As a producer, I want the triage logic to detect and suppress known phantom
patterns (mixed-tree verdicts from a moving checkout) so they no longer
auto-mint critical `test-failure` work items, while genuine failures still
triage normally.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **No phantom test-failure items:** after the mitigation, the race no longer
   generates additional phantom test-failure work items without manual triage;
   existing test-failure triage logic detects and suppresses known phantom
   patterns.
2. The test-failure triage helper detects known phantom signatures — a
   `state_changed_during_run` / mid-run fast-forward flag, or output recorded
   while the executing checkout was not a stable, pinned tree — and suppresses
   auto-creation of a `test-failure` work item, recording the suppression
   reason instead.
3. A suppressed phantom is still reported in the run's output/report with an
   explicit notice (`state_changed_during_run` notice code or equivalent),
   so the information is never silently lost — it is simply not minted as a
   critical item.
4. A genuine failure on a stable checkout still creates/updates a
   `test-failure` work item exactly as before (no behaviour change for real
   failures).
5. The suppression is covered by tests (both a phantom pattern that is
   suppressed and a genuine failure that is triaged).
6. The full project test suite passes with the change.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/triage/scripts/check_or_create.py` — the triage helper
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` —
  `_route_post_push_failure_to_triage` / `_post_push_failure_test_name`
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — F3 `_run_tests_via_test_skill`
  triage routing
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`, `skill/test_cache.py` —
  `state_changed_during_run` notice

## Constraints

- Existing triage behaviour for real failures must be preserved.
- Inverse: suppression must be conservative — never suppress when the failure
  may be genuine.
- Implementation repo: framework skills live in the SorraAgents repo
  (`~/.pi/agent/skills` → `/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/skill`); run
  `wl` worktree-safely with `--worklog-dir` when operating there.

## Goal

As a producer browsing the Herdr worklog selection list, I want the items that **block** a visible blocked item to also be **visible**, and in the **same group** as the blocked item, so that I can see (and dispatch) the work that must be finished before the blocked work can start — instead of seeing "blocked" rows whose blockers are nowhere in the list.

**Reported symptom (llm-proxy worklog):** `LP-0MW7V0S6A006DKZ4`, `LP-0MW7V14DN007F127` and `LP-0MVMHNUAR006SRZT` are visible in the Herdr selection list, but their blocking items are not visible anywhere in the list.

**Discovered from:** llm-proxy work items `LP-0MW7V0S6A006DKZ4` (Group 1 validation), `LP-0MW7V14DN007F127` (Group 2 validation) and `LP-0MVMHNUAR006SRZT` (Optimise llama-server prefill latency). Those ids are foreign to this store; they are listed only as evidence.

## Reproduction (measured 2026-11-08)

Selection list for the llm-proxy worklog (`/home/rgardler/projects/llm`), with `browseItemCount = 20` (`~/.config/herdr/worklog-plugin.json`):

| Visible blocked item | Stage | Active blocker(s) (status / stage / parent) |
|---|---|---|
| `LP-0MW7V0S6A006DKZ4` | intake_complete | `LP-0MW7V292T0020G02` open / intake_complete / **root**, `LP-0MW7V29MA009MCPI` open / intake_complete / **root** |
| `LP-0MW7V14DN007F127` | intake_complete | `LP-0MW7V2D13004ZO65` open / intake_complete / **root**, `LP-0MW7V2DK400365ER` open / intake_complete / **root**, `LP-0MW7V0S6A006DKZ4` (blocked — already visible) |
| `LP-0MVMHNUAR006SRZT` | plan_complete | `LP-0MVNBJWG6006Z7YQ` open / intake_complete / **child of the blocked item** |
| `LP-0MW0KZVRX005VPMT` | idea | `LP-0MW7V14DN007F127` (blocked — already visible) |

Verified by driving the **real** functions against the live data: build the pipeline input from `wl worklist -n 20 --json` (browse feed + `critical`/`reviewQueue`/`inProgressRoots`/`blockedRoots` subsets, deduped by id), then call `selectWorkItems(merged, 20)` and `regroupWorkItems(selected)` from `packages/herdr/src/`. Result: **24 rows selected — 4 `blocked` rows plus 20 `In Review` rows — and every one of the three root blockers (`LP-0MW7V292T0020G02`, `LP-0MW7V29MA009MCPI`, `LP-0MVNBJWG6006Z7YQ`) absent (HIDDEN)**. Grouping of that output: the four blocked items each sat in their own group (`Group 1`, `Group 2`, `Group 3`, `Idea`), the 20 in_review rows in `In Review`.

## Root cause 1 — the browse window is fully consumed by the mandatory review queue

1. `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` (`fetcher` wrapper) calls `fetchNextItems(clampBrowseItemCount(settings.browseItemCount))` — 20 here; the plugin default is also 20.
2. `fetchNextItems` → `assembleDefaultWorklist` / `mergeMandatoryAndSelect` (`packages/herdr/src/fetcher.root-substitution.ts`) → `selectWorkItems(merged, count)`.
3. `selectWorkItems` (`packages/herdr/src/smart-selection.ts`) always includes the mandatory set (critical ∪ `status=in-progress` ∪ `status=blocked` ∪ completed `in_review`) and then fills only `othersLimit = max(0, count − mandatory.length)` slots with everything else.
4. **A blocker is only ever an "other".** `isMandatoryItem` never matches an `open` item, and nothing in the pipeline looks at dependency edges. With 20 root completed/in_review items + 4 blocked roots in this worklog, `othersLimit = 0`, so **every** non-mandatory item is cut — including every open blocker. (This is not blocker-specific: right now the window is entirely saturated by the review queue. The blocker case is the sharpest symptom because the blockers are the items the blocked rows are waiting on.)

## Root cause 2 — no blocker→blocked grouping rule

`groupItemsByFilePaths` (`packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts`) gives **every** item with no `Key Files` section its own singleton "restricted" group. None of the items in the table above has a `Key Files` section, so even if a blocker were selected it would land in a *different* group (and its own section heading) from the blocked item it blocks. There is no rule anywhere that associates a dependency edge with group membership: edges are read only for the metadata panel's `Blocked By` rows (`fetchBlockersForItem` / `fetchOutboundDepsForItems` in `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.api.ts`).

## Root cause 3 — a child blocker is excluded by the root-only top-level rule

`LP-0MVNBJWG6006Z7YQ` is a **child of the blocked item it blocks** (`LP-0MVMHNUAR006SRZT`). `selectWorkItems` drops every item with a non-empty `parentId` (root-only top level, `WL-0MS964SIA0057ABR` / `WL-0MVN4WESM007T4XI`), so that blocker is only reachable by expanding the parent — where it does render inside the parent's group.

**The fix must keep that rule.** A blocker that is a child is never promoted to the top level; it is represented by its **ROOT ancestor** (the same parent-substitution contract the critical-child path already implements — `substituteCriticalRoots` / `walkToRootAncestor` in `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.root-substitution.ts`, `WL-0MVN4WESM007T4XI`). When the child blocker's root ancestor *is* the blocked item itself (exactly the `LP-0MVMHNUAR006SRZT` → `LP-0MVNBJWG6006Z7YQ` case) substitution collapses to an item that is already visible: nothing is added, nothing is duplicated, and the child stays reachable through expand inside the parent's group.

## Scope

**In:** the Herdr **default** worklist selection + regroup pipeline (`smart-selection.ts`, `fetcher.root-substitution.ts`, `grouping.ts`, and the blocker read they reuse); the tests named below; the doc/comment updates that state the new guarantee.

**Out:**
- **Stage-filtered views** (`fetchItemsByStage`): these are deliberately narrow, so injecting a blocker whose stage falls outside the filter would be wrong. The new guarantee is documented as default-view only.
- **Any change to the "show parents, not children" rule itself.** Children are never rendered at the top level; a child blocker is represented by its root ancestor (see Root cause 3 and AC6).
- **The `browseItemCount` policy itself** (a deep review queue starving every "other" item). If that is judged worth changing, raise it as a separate `discovered-from` item — this item only guarantees blocker visibility.
- The Pi TUI Worklog extension (its grouping copy was removed by `WL-0MSGI7PV9004UD0N`).
- `wl` core CLI grouping/scoring — the fix is Herdr-side only.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Blocker visibility (the reported defect).** For a selection list built from the current live shape (20 root completed/in_review items, 4 blocked roots, `browseItemCount = 20`), every **active** blocker of a **visible** blocked item is represented in the returned list — as the blocker itself when it is a root item, or via its root ancestor when it is a child (AC6). A test reproduces the §Reproduction shape exactly (20 in_review + 4 blocked + open blockers) in `fetcher-worklist-bundle.test.ts` against a seeded real worklog DB, and asserts each root blocker id is selected — not merely "not dropped by the count window".
- **AC2 — Same group as the blocked item.** Each pinned blocker carries the *same* `group` and `groupLabel` as the blocked item it blocks, despite having no shared key files. If a blocker blocks two or more visible blocked items that land in different groups, it appears **exactly once, in the first (lowest-numbered) group in display order**.
- **AC3 — Adjacency.** Within the group, a pinned blocker is placed immediately after the blocked item it was pinned for (deterministic: the lowest-numbered group's blocked item when it blocks several), so a blocked row is always followed by its blockers. If implementation cost forces a downgrade to "same group, anywhere in it", record that decision in a comment on this item rather than silently dropping the requirement.
- **AC4 — No duplicates, no disappearances.** The selected list contains no duplicate ids (a blocker already selected in an earlier group is not re-added), and no item that is visible today becomes invisible as a result of the change (pin-only, never remove).
- **AC5 — No-op when nothing is blocked.** When no visible item has an active blocker, the selected list and its grouping are byte-identical to today's output (regression test over a fixture with no blocked items).
- **AC6 — "Show parents, not children" preserved by parent substitution.** A blocker that is a **child** of another item is never rendered at the top level. Instead its **ROOT ancestor** (walk `parentId` to the top-most non-child item) is what gets pinned into the blocked item's group, reusing the existing `walkToRootAncestor` / `substituteCriticalRoots` machinery rather than a second implementation. Tests must cover three cases:
  - **child blocker under a third-party parent** → the root is pinned and the child id never appears at top level;
  - **child blocker whose root is the blocked item itself** (`LP-0MVMHNUAR006SRZT` / `LP-0MVNBJWG6006Z7YQ`) → no row is added at all (the substitute is already visible), no duplicate, and the child is still reachable via expand of the parent;
  - **nested child blocker** → the TOP-MOST ancestor is pinned (mirroring the existing nested-critical-child test).
  Also assert no leftover `parentId` item appears in the selected list at all (a generalisation of the existing root-only assertion), and that the existing critical-child substitution tests (`packages/herdr/src/fetcher-worklist-bundle.test.ts`) still pass unchanged.
- **AC7 — One active-blocker predicate.** Pinning uses the shared `isActiveBlocker` predicate (`packages/herdr/src/fetcher.blockers.ts`) so the pinned set can never disagree with the metadata panel's `Blocked By` rows: `completed`/`deleted` targets and targets at stage `in_review`/`done` are **not** pinned. Test covers each terminal case.
- **AC8 — Read cost.** Pinning adds **no** new `wl` process spawn per visible blocked item on the default path: reuse the in-process outbound-dep read (`fetchOutboundDepsForItems`, one batched read over all selected blocked ids) or extend the consolidated `wl worklist` bundle. State the measured spawn count before/after for the default refresh (`packages/herdr/src/fetcher-spawn-cap.test.ts` / split-guard suites stay green).
- **AC9 — Content-determinism preserved.** Group assignment remains a pure function of item content + dependency edges, never of `updatedAt`/arrival order (`WL-0MVVLBTTP003Y4XO`): the same item set and edges always produce the same pinned grouping (test: shuffle the input, assert identical group numbers).
- **AC10 — Dispatch head stated and tested.** `getHerdrListHead` derives from the same selection, so pinning changes the dispatcher's candidate ranking. Record the intended effect (blockers become dispatchable from the list head) in a comment/doc, and cover it with a test so the ordering change is deliberate rather than incidental.
- **AC11 — Docs.** Update the mandatory-subset / selection documentation (`docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md`) and the header comments of `smart-selection.ts` / `grouping.ts` to state: blockers of a visible blocked item are always shown, in the blocked item's group, first group wins, default view only.
- **AC12 — Deliberate invariant override documented.** Pinning overrides the file-path conflict invariant for the blocker/blocked pair (two conflicting items can share a group). Add the inline comment explaining why, so a later reader does not "fix" it back.

## Decisions already taken

- **"First group in the list"** means the lowest `group` integer, i.e. display order.
- **A child blocker is represented by its parent, never itself** (AC6) — the rule is "show parents, not children". The replacement is the **root ancestor** (top-most item), matching the critical-child precedent, not merely the immediate parent; promoting the child would re-introduce the duplicated-row bug that `WL-0MS964SIA0057ABR` / `WL-0MVN4WESM007T4XI` removed. Where the substituted root is the blocked item itself the pin is a no-op (no duplicate row).
- **Pinning beats file-path packing** for the blocker/blocked pair (the user requirement), documented per AC12.
- Only **direct** blockers are pinned. A pinned blocker that is itself blocked is not chased transitively unless it is already mandatory — keep the rule simple and documented; transitive closure can be a follow-up if it proves necessary.

## Problem statement

A herdr instance whose downtime dispatch is switched off (`downtimeEnabled: false`, or the manual `d` disable marker) produces **no coordination offer at all**, because the tick short-circuits before the check-in:

```ts
// packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.orchestrator-tick.ts:80-85
if (!(ctx.override ?? cfg.enabled)) {
  ctx.activeAuditBatch = null;
  return { polled: false, dispatched: false, idle: false };  // no check-in, no offer
}
```

The elected leader therefore cannot see that root's backlog. The only current remedy is to hand-register the root in `downtimeWorklogRoots` (`WL-0MVR8GDJ3008WY3Y`), which duplicates a source of truth the instance already knows: operators must remember to register every root whose local instance is deliberately non-dispatching, and a stale registry silently strands work.

Typical deployments that hit this: a desktop instance that must not run agents locally (no local model capacity, contested GPU, machine in use), and a laptop instance kept only as a viewer.

## Users

- **Operators** running a herdr instance that must never dispatch locally but whose worklog root should still be served by the fleet leader. *As an operator, I want my instance to advertise the work it can see without ever spawning a pane itself, so I do not have to maintain a separate registry of roots.*
- **The elected leader** — needs a candidate list that includes roots whose local instance is present-but-passive. *As the dispatcher, I want passive instances to contribute offers so I can allocate idle capacity wherever it exists.*

## Desired change

A new setting `downtimeOfferOnly` (default `false`). When dispatch is disabled and `downtimeOfferOnly` is `true`, the tick performs the leader-election check-in and the offer computation only:

- computes and writes/refreshes this instance's coordination entry (`computeMostImportantItem`, existing filters, existing staleness semantics);
- does **not** poll the local proxy for capacity, does **not** take the leader lease, does **not** claim an item, write a dispatch marker, or spawn a pane.

When dispatch is disabled and `downtimeOfferOnly` is `false` (the default), behaviour is unchanged: no check-in, no offer.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Mode exists and is off by default.** `downtimeOfferOnly: boolean` (default `false`) is added to `PluginSettings`, clamped/validated and loaded like every other downtime knob (`packages/herdr/src/settings.ts`), and re-read each tick so the setting applies without a plugin restart.
- [ ] **AC2 — Offer-only instance checks in and offers.** With dispatch disabled (either `downtimeEnabled: false` or a live manual disable marker) and `downtimeOfferOnly: true`, one tick writes/refreshes the instance's coordination entry with its computed offer and updates `lastUpdated` on the normal check-in cadence.
- [ ] **AC3 — Offer-only instance never dispatches.** In the same tick the proxy-status poll, leader-lease acquisition, CAS claim, dispatch-marker write, host-budget reservation and pane spawn are all not called (asserted against the injected deps/seams in tests).
- [ ] **AC4 — No behaviour change otherwise.** (a) dispatch enabled ⇒ unchanged, whatever `downtimeOfferOnly` says; (b) dispatch disabled + `downtimeOfferOnly: false` ⇒ unchanged (no check-in, no entry); pinned by tests for both.
- [ ] **AC5 — Fail-open.** An offer computation or coordination write that fails leaves the previous entry intact (existing `computeMostImportantItem` `{ok:false}` contract), never throws out of the tick and never removes another instance's entry.
- [ ] **AC6 — Leader-side compatibility.** The leader's existing dispatch-time re-validation (`fetchItem` → `classifyItemForDispatch` → gates) and its 24 h `hasPeerOffer` liveness predicate are unchanged; an offer from a passive instance is indistinguishable from an active one at dispatch time, so no leader change is required.
- [ ] **AC7 — Tests.** Unit tests for the four enabled/offer-only combinations; a tick-level test proving no capacity poll / no claim / no spawn; and one leader-side test that an offer written by a disabled+offer-only instance is dispatched (with a stubbed spawn) even though that instance has no capacity.
- [ ] **AC8 — Docs.** `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` (the enabled/disable gate section and the composition summary) and `packages/herdr/README.md` document the mode, its default, and when to prefer it over `downtimeWorklogRoots`.
- [ ] **AC9 — Gate.** Full project test suite passes via the dev-push gate; no existing downtime test is weakened.

## Existing state

- `applyEnabledGates()` (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.orchestrator-tick.ts:76-106`) returns before leader election/check-in when dispatch is disabled; the manual disable marker takes the same early return.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts:1757` wires `enabled: s.downtimeEnabled`; the effective state is `ctx.override ?? cfg.enabled` (`downtime-worker.orchestrator.ts:211-216`).
- The offer computation already exists and is transport-agnostic: `computeMostImportantItem` (`downtime-worker.coordination.ts:153`) returns one item (or `{ok:false}`); the check-in write lives on the leader/peer path (`runCoordinationCheckIn`).
- One entry per instance, machine-wide file at `~/.herdr/downtime/downtime-coordination.json` (`coordination.ts`, `COORDINATION_FILE_VERSION = 1`).

## Constraints

- No change to the election protocol, the lease TTL, the entry schema or the offer→dispatch contract — this adds a passive participant, it does not add a second selection path.
- Offer-only is strictly a check-in concern: it must be impossible for a passive instance to dispatch, claim, reserve or lead (fail closed in code, not by convention).
- No dependency on `downtimeWorklogRoots`: the two mechanisms must be independently usable and independently documentable.
- All written output in UK English.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk (low): the entry masks an empty root.** A passive instance whose root has nothing dispatchable writes an entry whose offer is refused at dispatch time (already handled: stale offers are dropped via `removeEntry`, never a strike).
- **Risk (medium): capacity polling side effects.** Ensure the "no proxy poll" requirement is enforced structurally (the tick returns before the poller is constructed/called), not by an early `return` that a later refactor can reorder.
- **Assumption:** an offer written by a passive instance is valid even though that instance has no local capacity, because admission is decided by the leader on the dispatching host.
- **Scope-creep guard:** per-tier (multi-offer) nomination is a separate item; this item keeps one offer per instance.

## Related work

- `WL-0MVR8GDJ3008WY3Y` — Downtime leader cannot see a worklog root with no running herdr instance (the `downtimeWorklogRoots` registry this item reduces the need for).
- `WL-0MST3OJ8S0001ROL` — single-leader downtime dispatch model (election + coordination file).
- Discovered during: 2026-11-12 dispatch stall analysis (implement budget 2/2 held by two provider-error panes; audit tier fail-closed on a missing proxy endpoint; ContextHub plan/intake work unreachable).

## Impact

Operators can keep a herdr instance in view-only mode and still have its root's work dispatched by the fleet leader, without maintaining a separate registry.

## Problem statement

An audit offer refused by the proxy-derived audit budget is **attributable, then discarded**. In `dispatchFromCoordination` the offer loop only records implement-tier budget refusals:

```ts
// packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.coordination-leader.ts
if (outcome.reason === 'host-budget-implement' || outcome.reason === 'host-budget-unknown') {
  hostBudgetHold ??= outcome;   // recorded
  continue;
}
```

An audit refusal returns `audit-budget-unknown` / `audit-budget-saturated` from `admitHostDispatch` (`host-dispatch-budget.admission.ts`, `admitAuditDispatch`), matches none of the special cases, and falls through. The terminal-reason chain then reports whatever `hostBudgetHold` holds — so the decision log says `host-budget-implement` while the actual reason the audit tier is dead is a **missing proxy endpoint**.

Observed 2026-11-12: the dispatcher logged 130 consecutive `host-budget-implement` ticks and **zero** `audit-budget-*` entries in any root's decision log, while:

```
$ curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' http://192.168.0.199:8000/llama/local/audit/status   → 404
$ curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' http://192.168.0.199:8000/llama/local/audit           → 404
$ curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' http://192.168.0.199:8000/llama/local/budget          → 404
$ curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' http://192.168.0.199:8000/llama/local/status          → 200
```

`decideAuditAvailability` maps `endpoint-absent (http-404)` to `{active: true, reason: 'audit-budget-unknown', detail: 'http-404'}`, so every audit on every host is refused — invisibly. An operator reading the log concludes "the implement budget is full, wait" and never learns that the review queue cannot drain at all.

## Users

- **Operators** triaging a dispatch stall. *As an operator, I want the decision log to name the gate that actually stopped each tier, with the failing exchange, so I do not chase the wrong budget.*
- **The dispatcher itself** — needs the audit hold to participate in terminal-reason precedence instead of being silently dropped.

## Desired change

1. Record audit-tier refusals as their own neutral hold (for example `auditBudgetHold`, mirroring `hostBudgetHold`), carrying `reason` and `detail`.
2. Fold that hold into the terminal-reason precedence at a position that reflects severity — an audit refusal with `detail: 'http-404'` is a *broken contract*, not an ambient budget statement, so it must not be masked by `host-budget-implement`. Documented precedence: `code-freeze` → CPU → review-queue → non-terminal cooldown → attempt budget → in-flight → leaf-audit pin → **audit budget** → host budget → `no-candidate`.
3. Emit the audit refusal's `detail` (the failing exchange: `http-404`, `timeout`, `network`, `bad-body`, `seam-absent`) in the same decision entry, so the log is self-explanatory without reading code.
4. Keep every existing neutral-hold contract: no strike, no cooldown, no attempt-budget charge, offer entries kept, no pane.
5. Extend the same treatment to the per-offer rejection attribution (`withOfferRejections` / gate tokens) so `audit-budget-*` appears in the attribution payload of every tick that has an audit offer.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Every audit refusal is recorded.** A refused audit offer sets a hold carrying its reason and detail; a tick whose only refusal is an audit refusal reports an `audit-budget-*` terminal reason (never `host-budget-implement`, never `no-candidate`).
- [ ] **AC2 — Precedence fixed and documented.** The documented chain gains the audit-budget rung above the host-budget rung; `docs/dev/downtime-worker` module contract comments (the "Continuable holds and terminal-reason precedence" block) are updated to match, and a test asserts the relative order of an audit hold and an implement hold in the same tick.
- [ ] **AC3 — Detail is surfaced.** The decision entry for an audit refusal carries the failing exchange detail; a test covers `http-404`, `timeout` and `bad-body`.
- [ ] **AC4 — Neutral contract preserved.** No strike, no cooldown, no attempt-budget flag, coordination entry kept (tests assert each).
- [ ] **AC5 — Attribution payload.** `withOfferRejections` output for an audit refusal includes the audit gate token, so a single tick explains every offer it skipped.
- [ ] **AC6 — Mirrored on the direct path.** If the direct (`dispatchDowntimeWork`) path drops audit refusals the same way, it is fixed identically; if it does not, a test pins its existing behaviour and the difference is recorded in the item.
- [ ] **AC7 — Regression.** Unit tests for: audit-only refusal; audit + implement refusal in one tick (precedence); audit refusal alongside a successful dispatch (hold must not pollute the success outcome).
- [ ] **AC8 — Docs and gate.** `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` decision-reason table lists the audit tokens; full project test suite passes via the dev-push gate.

## Existing state

- `dispatchFromCoordination` — special cases for `host-budget-implement` / `host-budget-unknown`, `claim-failed`, `claim-rolled-back`, `wl-error`, `anchor-unavailable`, `spawn-failed`, `marker-write-failed`; no audit-budget case (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.coordination-leader.ts`).
- `admitAuditDispatch` — returns `reason: decision.reason` (`audit-budget-saturated` / `audit-budget-unknown`) with `live`/`max` evidence (`host-dispatch-budget.admission.ts`).
- `AUDIT_BUDGET_SATURATED_REASON` / `AUDIT_BUDGET_UNKNOWN_REASON` / `AuditAvailabilityOutcome` arms (`downtime-worker.audit-availability.contract.ts`, `downtime-worker.audit-availability.ts`).
- Terminal-reason chain: `downtime-worker.coordination-leader.ts` (frozen → cpu → review → cooldown → attempt → in-flight → pin → host budget → no-candidate).
- Grep evidence from the incident: no `audit-budget-` string in any `*/.worklog/downtime-coordination.log*`.

## Constraints

- Reporting and precedence only: no change to admission, to the proxy contract, or to which dispatches are admitted.
- No new strike/cooldown path — the hold stays neutral so a broken endpoint cannot spiral the worker into pause.
- All written output in UK English.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk (low): log-volume noise.** A permanently broken audit endpoint would log an audit-budget reason every idle tick. Mitigated because the tick is already logging a no-dispatch reason every poll; the value is that the reason becomes correct.
- **Risk (medium): precedence bikeshedding.** The rung order is a contract; capture it in the module doc comment and a test rather than in prose only.
- **Assumption:** `audit-budget-unknown` with `http-404` is operationally a *configuration/proxy-contract* failure and deserves to outrank an ambient implement-cap refusal. If the producer disagrees, only the rung position changes, not the recording.
- **Related but not in scope:** the missing `/llama/local/audit/status` endpoint itself (proxy repo, sibling item `LP-0MW95FYMH006XYNK`), and setting `HERDR_AUDIT_LOCAL_BUDGET=1` as the one-release escape hatch.

## Related work

- `LP-0MW95FYMH006XYNK` — the proxy endpoint the audit gate depends on (missing in the incident).
- `WL-0MWAMSDNW000SL0E` / `WL-0MWAMSK9H005BOHD` — proxy-derived audit admission and its decision logging.
- `WL-0MWBT76WY00298AY` — continuable hold predicate and terminal-reason precedence (the contract this extends).
- `WL-0MVR8FKMU009XTED` — per-offer rejection attribution.
- Discovered during: 2026-11-12 dispatch stall analysis (implement cap 2/2 held by two provider-error panes, audit tier fail-closed on a 404, ~130 ticks misattributed).

## Impact

Operators reading the dispatcher log are told the true reason a tier is stalled — including a missing proxy endpoint — instead of a misleading implement-budget message.
